### What is the purpose of your *pull request*?
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Improvement
- [ ] New extractor
- [ ] New feature

---

### Description of your *pull request* and other information

I've added login support for Tumblr. Some time in the last year, Tumblr has made it impossible to download explicit content without logging in. When you try to view explicit content without being logged in, you're redirected to a splash screen (https://www.tumblr.com/safe-mode?url=...) which youtube-dl then passes to the generic downloader. This results in HTML pages being downloaded with weird names, such as "safe-mode-168487385934.unknown_video"

The addition of login support allows these URLs to be downloaded without issue. I've tested this locally with both the regular `--username` and `--password` flags and the ~/.netrc file and `-n` flag.

I'm not a Python developer by trade, so please excuse the code if it's a bit off. I believe the code passes flake8 - I ran `flake8 tumblr.py` locally and there wasn't any output.

### Description of your *pull request* and other information

I've added login support for Tumblr. Some time in the last year, Tumblr has made it impossible to download explicit content without logging in. When you try to view explicit content without being logged in, you're redirected to a splash screen (https://www.tumblr.com/safe-mode?url=...) which youtube-dl then passes to the generic downloader. This results in HTML pages being downloaded with weird names, such as "safe-mode-168487385934.unknown_video"

The addition of login support allows these URLs to be downloaded without issue. I've tested this locally with both the regular `--username` and `--password` flags and the ~/.netrc file and `-n` flag.

I'm not a Python developer by trade, so please excuse the code if it's a bit off. I believe the code passes flake8 - I ran `flake8 tumblr.py` locally and there wasn't any output.

Please let me know if there's anything else I can do to improve the code. ### Description of your *pull request* and other information

I've added login support for Tumblr. Some time in the last year, Tumblr has made it impossible to download explicit content without logging in. When you try to view explicit content without being logged in, you're redirected to a splash screen (https://www.tumblr.com/safe-mode?url=...) which youtube-dl then passes to the generic downloader. This results in HTML pages being downloaded with weird names, such as "safe-mode-168487385934.unknown_video"

The addition of login support allows these URLs to be downloaded without issue. I've tested this locally with both the regular `--username` and `--password` flags and the ~/.netrc file and `-n` flag.

I'm not a Python developer by trade, so please excuse the code if it's a bit off. I believe the code passes flake8 - I ran `flake8 tumblr.py` locally and there wasn't any output.

Please let me know if there's anything else I can do to improve the code. ### Description of your *pull request* and other information

I've added login support for Tumblr. Some time in the last year, Tumblr has made it impossible to download explicit content without logging in. When you try to view explicit content without being logged in, you're redirected to a splash screen (https://www.tumblr.com/safe-mode?url=...) which youtube-dl then passes to the generic downloader. This results in HTML pages being downloaded with weird names, such as "safe-mode-168487385934.unknown_video"

The addition of login support allows these URLs to be downloaded without issue. I've tested this locally with both the regular `--username` and `--password` flags and the ~/.netrc file and `-n` flag.

I'm not a Python developer by trade, so please excuse the code if it's a bit off. I believe the code passes flake8 - I ran `flake8 tumblr.py` locally and there wasn't any output.

Please let me know if there's anything else I can do to improve the code. I don't like how the current artificial horizon is fixed on the x-axis and can only travel up and down. When the aircraft rolls, the horizon becomes larger in its overall length, and it only supports rolls to a certain angle. If you go above that angle, it get's stuck at its max angle and you don't get any usefull roll information from it.

In real fighter jets and helicopters the artificial horizon is often perpendicular to and centered to the shortest line between aircraft direction and horizon.
I tried to implement that and here is how it looks with the Betaflight OSD

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o3BrLwBB_iE

Notice how you can roll at any angle without the horizon getting stuck.
I added an error pointing at the shortest way to the horizon if the horizon gets far away from the screen center or even out of the screen.

The downside is that resolution on the x-axis is limited to the width of a char. That means that if you fly knife edge, the pitch movement would not have such a fine resolution on the horizon as if you fly level or inverted.

I like this approach alot more, because this is how I know it from DCS or Arma.


Some other aspects which I would like to see in general are the following two:
*Let the user adjust at least the Y-position of the crosshair/level horizon if they fly with camera tilt.
*Let the user adjust the "sensitivity" of the horizon pitch movement. This way the user could set it so that the artificial horizon is always where the real horizon is in the camera image (as it would be in a real fighter aircraft)."},"comment":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/betaflight/betaflight/issues/comments/354648017","html_url":"https://github.com/betaflight/betaflight/issues/4882#issuecomment-354648017","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/betaflight/betaflight/issues/4882","id":354648017,"user":{"login":"DanNixon","id":4037377,"avatar_url":"https://avatars0.githubusercontent.com/u/4037377?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon","html_url":"https://github.com/DanNixon","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/DanNixon/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2018-01-01T11:11:00Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:11:00Z","author_association":"NONE","body":"> *Let the user adjust at least the Y-position of the crosshair/level horizon if they fly with camera tilt.

+ ##My Google Code In Experience
+
+I am Swastik Das, a  student of class XI at SAI International School, Bhubaneswar, India.
+I heard about Google Code In from Sampriti Panda who has participated in GCI trice earlier and has also been the Grand prize Winner last year.
+From childhood computer have fascinated me. I love everything related to them let it be gaming, editing stuffs or coding.
+This year I decided to participate in the GCI.
+I chose JBoss Community on reading that it is related to Java.
+I got to learn about many open-source softwares. They are great to work with. You can use them and also modify and upgrade those softwares which is a great thing.
+I learnt how to develop apps, integrate authentication methods, designing webpages and various other stuffs.
+At present I know Java, Javascript, C++, C#, Swift, HTML, CSS and I would love to learn more and master in these programming languages too.
+
+##Mentors
+The mentors are really good and cooperative.
+They check all our works and also advice us on improving our programming skills and also to rectify to mistakes.
+They are really friendly and never step back in clearing doubts or helping in any other ways.

`readme.md` files are written with a strict line length in most of the cases. You can look at the raw file [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/exercism/python/master/exercises/simple-cipher/README.md) to get an idea.

When I clone and try to open in an editor. I usually prefer to keep the code on one side and the readme on another. Since its a lot of text its breaking up more than necessary because of the newlines.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2767425/34467236-550d59d2-ef11-11e7-8163-716f738c133f.png)

Can we ignore the line length convention in the readme files ? Hope I made myself clear. Let me know your opinions. Will be happy to do a pr fixing those.

Happy new year 🙂 "}}

该方法用于Windows系统，不保证100%有用。

1.到灯笼官网（https://getlantern.org/en_US/）下载最新正式版本的安装程序，下载后别着急安装。也可以通过其它渠道获取最新正式版，但请注意安全。
2.把你使用的设备与专业版账号解绑。（如果你系统里没有安装灯笼，或无法打开灯笼的菜单，那么可以忽略）
3.卸载系统中已安装的灯笼。（如果没有安装，请忽略）
4.删除C:\Users\AppData\Roaming\Lantern文件夹。该文件夹为隐藏属性。
5.将系统的首选DNS地址改为8.8.8.8  备选DNS地址改为8.8.4.4
6.重启计算机；或者打开cmd.exe ，执行 ipconfig/flushdns 命令，以此来清除DNS缓存。酱紫你就可以不重启
7.关闭系统中的任何防毒软件、防火墙软件
8.以管理员身份运行已下载的灯笼安装程序
9.把你使用的设备与专业版账号绑定
10.将C:\Users\AppData\Roaming\Lantern文件夹添加到防毒软件的排除项目（信任区）之中。


我建议大家使用卡巴斯基作为系统的防毒软件，Google Chrome作为系统的默认浏览器。
现在卡巴斯基推出了免费版，度娘搜索 卡巴斯基免费版 即可下载。免费版无防火墙功能，如果你还需要一个防火墙，推荐升级到 卡巴斯基安全软件 或者使用 TripMode 。如果不想钱包变瘪，使用Windows内置的防火墙也是一个不错的选择。"}}

same working between mycli and pgcli about substiting parameters in favorite queries.

sample of usage

```

> \ns test select * from test where id=%s

+------+-------+

| id   | lib   |
|------+-------|

+------+-------+
```

ttps://github.com/Louie5","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Louie5/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2018-01-01T11:12:34Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:12:34Z","author_association":"OWNER","body":"Q9：先读哪些？再读哪些？

答: 选了一堆经典读物，先读哪一本？后读哪一本呢？建议如下：

先读最薄的书。历史上更能流传下来的书都是薄书。为什么？人类大脑的工作原理是能偷懒就偷懒，不该偷懒的时候还要偷懒。比如儒家经典《论语》与《孟子》，《孟子》共38125字，全文十一篇，从2877字到6524字不等。反之，《论语》的总字数为15900字，全文二十篇，从370字到1340字不等。《孟子》的书比《论语》厚，但结果是《论语》比《孟子》传播的更广。

先读近一点的书。假设面前两本经典都是五十年前的著作，一本成书于1910年；一本成书于1970年。那么，就挑离当代近一点的读，先读1970年。可以参考阅读桑兵老师主编的《读书法》一书，虽然主要此书主要谈的是如何培养历史系硕博阅读习惯，收录了众多大儒谈如何读书，但此书的不少观点，可以拓展到其他领域。桑兵老师为此书写的序「大众时代的小众读书法」，讲读书方法讲得很通透。比如读阳明心学，与刘宗周相比，你更容易与钱穆梁启超产生共鸣。

先读文笔优美的书。大脑偏好美，美也是一种生产力。先挑选作者文笔优美的书，如果是译本，也尽量挑选一本译笔优美的书。以认知科学为例，平克文笔比斯坦诺维奇好，那么，如果时间有限，只能先读一个人的，就先读平克的。

先读历史有定论的书。不要从哗众取宠的作品入手。这些作品因为争议，更容易影响那些知识根基不深的新人。误以为某某学科就是这样了。你一定要先读历史上有公论，能传承文化的那些书，比如进化论读《物种起源》与《自私的基因》。"}}

I'm going to push back a bit on allowing RegExp's ... most combinators are just a single special character (+, ~) and I don't see this feature being all that useful.

That's a fair point. I originally intended to add RegExps for controlling the what whitespace is allowed for descendant combinators. I've updated the tests and examples to show this, rather than use the child and piercing combinators.

> I'm thinking that POSSIBLY -whitelist should assume " " is a valid combinator and add it automatically to the config?

I think there is a use case for not allowing the descendant combinator e.g. a completely flat specificity graph or when (exclusively) using CSS Modules' `composes` system.

Having said all that, perhaps it is better to split this up:

- `selector-descendant-combinator-no-non-space` (already built)
- `selector-no-descendent-combinator`
- `selector-combinator-blacklist`
- `selector-combinator-whitelist`

The latter two would ignore whitespace descendant combinators and not accept RegExp.

What do you think?

Description

Allows fallback videos to be used for download, when the main video URL is not downloadable (e.g., HLS .m3u8).

**JIRA**

[OSPR-2019](https://openedx.atlassian.net/browse/OSPR-2019)

Allows the streaming video URL to differ from the download URL.  Iterates through the `all_sources` HTML5 video URLs to locate a downloadable video URL, if the streaming video URL is not downloadable.

### Notes

Functionality depends on API changes in https://github.com/edx/edx-platform/pull/16590, but the app continues to work even if this change is not deployed yet.

Builds on https://github.com/edx/edx-app-ios/pull/1014, which differentiates between streamable and downloadable video URLs.

We'd like to get this merged before the next edx-app-ios release.

### How to test this PR

Ensure that the changes from https://github.com/edx/edx-platform/pull/16590 are running in your LMS, and import this [video_test_course.tar.gz](https://github.com/edx/edx-app-ios/files/1493756/video_test_course.Dl2Kjh.tar.gz), which contains permutations of all the various video streaming/download scenarios.

Alternately, run against this sandbox server, using:
```yaml
API_HOST_URL: 'https://pr16590.sandbox.opencraft.hosting'
OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: '14cdc120d61349b7eeba'
```

1. Run the iOS app.
1. Login as a student to the test course.
1. Visit each of the course subsections in turn, noting the expected Streaming and Download behaviours for each unit below.
    *note* Once you've downloaded a video, that video will be used in the player, regardless of what the original streaming video URL is.  So to test the permutations below, try streaming first, then download.

* YouTube:
    * Standard: YouTube 
        * Streaming: YouTube only; will not play on iOS app, but will play in browser.
        * Download: none
    * Standard w Fallback:  
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 (same as MP4 - 1), different from YouTube video
        * Download: yes, same as stream
    * HLS live stream:
        * Streaming: YouTube only; will not play on iOS app, but will play in browser.
        * Download: none
    * HLS w fallback:
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 (same as MP4 - 1)
            *Note* The main video is configured to use the same YouTube HLS used in the previous unit, but `USING_VIDEO_PIPELINE: false` causes the fallback URL to be streamed instead.
        * Download: Same as stream.
* MP4 
    * MP4 - 1
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
    * MP4 - 1 w fallback
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
            *Note* Fallback video is configured to be the 0:27 mp4 used by MP4 - 2, but because the main video 
            can be downloaded, the fallback video is ignored.
    * MP4 - 2
        * Streaming: 0:27 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
    * MP4 - 2 w fallback
        * Streaming: 0:27 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
            *note* Fallback video is configured to be the 0:05 mp4 used by MP4 - 1, but because the main video 
            can be downloaded, the fallback video is ignored.
* HLS .m3u8
    * HLS (10 min):
        * Streaming: 10:35 video
        * Download: none
    * HLS (10 min) w fallback:
        * Streaming: 10:35 video
        * Download: 0:27 mp4, same as MP4 - 2
    * Vimeo
        * Streaming: 8:22 Cloudera m3mu
        * Download: none
    * Vimeo w fallback
        * Streaming: 8:22 Cloudera m3mu
        * Download: 8:22 Cloudera mp4

a lot of the unit support built into Matplotlib, and quite a lot of the internals, works on lists of unit-like object. This lets a list of quantities be converted fine using the Matplotlib unit converters in Astropy.

As an example, this change makes vlines and hlines work in Matplotlib:

```python
from astropy.visualization import quantity_support
import astropy.units as u
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

quantity_support()
x = 0.5 * u.m

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.axhline(x)

* https://docs.travis-ci.com/user/deployment/releases/
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/12343452/how-to-publish-artifacts-in-travis-ci/33109519#33109519

Islamic Lectures and Classical Books for English-speaking Muslims.

Ikhbāt Al-Qulūb is a volunteer-driven project to call to the creed of the Prophets (عليهم الصلاة والسلام) and the companions (رضي الله عنهم) through knowledge that is based on the Qurʾān and Sunnah. By providing the opportunity to learn and call to Islam simultaneously, in particular through the sharing of notes on books and lectures by students, we hope to help Muslims in their obligation to seek knowledge of the religion of Allah. Register for a richer experience and the ability to plan your studies, track your progress and submit notes.
 
Subscribe
Subscribe to our blog and follow our social media accounts to receive updates on the project and beneficial reminders.
	
Share
Spread the lectures, books, notes, and posts you like. Remind your family and friends of the obligation to seek beneficial knowledge and introduce them to Ikhbāt Al-Qulūb. Schedule a regular meeting time and study together.
	
Advise
Submit reports of errors you encounter and general feedback on how we can improve the learning experience of our visitors.

Study
Learn and facilitate learning at the same time by writing detailed notes on books and lectures. Improve the automatically generated English captions or provide translations for our videos on YouTube.

Proofread
Proofread submitted lecture notes to ensure consistent quality and enable conversion into dynamic lecture videos and quizzes.
	
Design
Promote the creed of the Prophets (عليهم الصلاة والسلام) and the companions to a wider audience on social media by bolstering our graphics with professional, picture-quotes and infographics.
	
Edit
Simplify the learning of your brothers and sisters by creating dynamic lecture videos with step-by-step outlines, or remind them through succinct reminders.

Code
Help us expand this platform with more features and mobile applications.

* Privatize and improve event / trigger pref

`getEvents` and `getTriggers` have no public purpose.
I also added some guards if there are no events defined.

Additionally there are two breaking changes.  Handlers for `childViewEvents` must now be defined prior to `delegateEvents`  This will match every other events related API.  If someone needs to add a `childViewEvents` handle after the fact, they'll need to re-call `delegateEvents`.
This should significantly improve perf in some cases.

Similarly `childViewEventPrefix` is now determined along with `childViewTriggers` and `childViewEvents` instead of on each triggered event.  This is another small breaking change. I personally believe we should focus more on native navigation so we can have a native side that would do navigation (iOS 11,  Android shared element transition and other iPhone X features) job automatically instead of having to make all these workarounds. Otherwise, we will be left behind than the native developers."},"comment":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/react-navigation/react-navigation/issues/comments/354648141","html_url":"https://github.com/react-navigation/react-navigation/issues/3205#issuecomment-354648141","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/react-navigation/react-navigation/issues/3205","id":354648141,"user":{"login":"satya164","id":1174278,"avatar_url":"https://avatars2.githubusercontent.com/u/1174278?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164","html_url":"https://github.com/satya164","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/satya164/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2018-01-01T11:14:47Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:14:47Z","author_association":"COLLABORATOR","body":""Finding better solution for navigation" is not an easy task. If it was, lots of people would have done already. Unless you have a bunch of talented devs having free time to build another navigation solution, it's not very productive approach as well. A better approach would be to discuss the pain points you have with this library, and how we can solve them. I already attempted https://github.com/react-navigation/react-navigation/issues/3195, comments are welcome.

> I personally believe we should focus more on native navigation so we can have a native side that would do navigation

This is debatable. Building it in native doesn't essentially make it better. I'm not against building solutions in native, and I had written my thoughts about it https://blog.callstack.io/why-you-should-not-re-implement-native-features-in-react-native-c699a70be76c

> iOS 11, Android shared element transition and other iPhone X features

Which iOS 11 and iPhone X features are you referring to? The notch, space for home button etc. are already handled.

Regarding shared transitions. It's not very difficult to build in React Native, and I don't believe that the feature has to be built into a navigation library. It's totally possible to build a custom navigator for React Navigation which handles shared transitions instead of building it into StackNavigator, which is overcomplicating things IMO.

Building a navigation library in native isn't an easy task. And even when you build it, there are several things involved to actually make it a good solution. If you are looking for a native navigation library, you already have https://github.com/wix/react-native-navigation. But they have been rewriting it for v2 for quite a long time. There is also https://github.com/airbnb/native-navigation, which seems to be abandoned."}}

{"action":"created","issue":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/mtesseract/nakadi-client/issues/56","repository_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/mtesseract/nakadi-client","labels_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/mtesseract/nakadi-client/issues/56/labels{/name}","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/mtesseract/nakadi-client/issues/56/comments","events_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/mtesseract/nakadi-client/issues/56/events","html_url":"https://github.com/mtesseract/nakadi-client/issues/56","id":285227752,"number":56,"title":"Generalizing callback monad and redesigning API","user":{"login":"mtesseract","id":11706080,"avatar_url":"https://avatars0.githubusercontent.com/u/11706080?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract","html_url":"https://github.com/mtesseract","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/mtesseract/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"labels":[],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignee":null,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":0,"created_at":"2017-12-30T22:33:43Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:15:16Z","closed_at":null,"author_association":"OWNER","body":"## This is the first part of a major API redesign.

Note that the current API has never been declared stable.

I suggest to work on this for a future 0.5.0.0 release.
@etorreborre @vitold @amrhassan 

### What is wrong with the current API?

Several things are not perfect, but let's focus on one aspect for now. Namely, all callbacks registered by the user in the Nakadi configuration are to be run in the `IO` monad. This is not a strict limitation, but an inconvenience, as the user might be using some more complicated monad stack on top of `IO` for an application. Nakadi requiring callbacks in the `IO` monad therefore means that the user might has to do some type conversion, e.g. by unwrapping the custom monad stack, before providing the callbacks to nakadi-client.

### What would be nicer?

It would be nicer if the user could decide for some custom "base monad" in which the callbacks are to be run. As these callbacks are stored in the Nakadi configuration value `Config`, this value needs to be parameterized by this `base` monad. [Note, there is some conflict in terminology here. What is often called 'base monad' in Haskell (see e.g. the `transformers-base` package), is a specific monad among `STM`, `IO`, `Maybe`, etc..  Something like

    type App a = ReaderT IO a

would not be a 'base monad'. This is different in the usage of the word within nakadi-client. A base monad here means 'the custom monad transformer stack for your application'. Thus, `ReaderT IO` could be a base monad, if that is what the callbacks produce.

As mentioned previously, the `Config` type would now be parameterized by some base monad `b`. So, a nakadi-client function could look as follows:

```
eventTypesList :: SomeConstraints b => Config' b -> b [EventType]
```

But this would be a bad API, as this would mean that the only monad in which nakadi-client calls could be executed would be the application's base monad `b`. For example, consuming events, requires a `MonadResource` constraint on the monad to run in. More generally speaking, the user should always be free to locally run in some other monad stack — as long as it has the same base monad at the bottom. Otherwise we couldn't call the user's callbacks without unlifting them.

To sumarize the above: We need at least two monads `b` and `m` and a 'sub-monad' relationship between them. Thus, we end up with something like this: 
```
eventTypesList :: (MonadSub b m, ...) => Config' b -> m [EventType]
```

In the above, we actually need some more type class constraints on `b` and `m`, namely `MonadIO m`, `MonadIO b`, `MonadCatch m` and `MonadMask b`. 

Currently, the nakadi-client package exposes basically two sets of API calls:

- Those, which require the Nakadi configuration to be given as first argument and

- those, which expect the Nakadi configuration to be implicitely available (currently, these are suffixed with 'R').

The current mechanism by which the implicit configuration was made available consisted of two parts:

- the `HasNakadiConfig` type class is defined and provided by nakadi-client

- the user implements this type class for some reader monad type in which the nakadi-client '*R' functions are used.

Sadly this way of doing things no longer works when the configuration is parameterized by the base monad, as this means that the `b` type cannot be uniquely inferred anymore: Given some monad stack involving several layers, there are many potential ways to slice this monad stack into a base monad and the rest. One would have to provide a `Proxy b` argument or something similar ugly to make type checker happy — clearly not an option.

### Approach

So, how we can we make it work instead? I have tried to go with the following solution:

- Define a modified and specialized `ReaderT` monad transformer named `NakadiT`:

```
newtype NakadiT b m a = NakadiT { _runNakadiT :: Config' b -> m a }
```

- Define the type class `MonadNakadiEnv` which defines the API for working with implicitely stored Nakadi configurations:

```
class SomeConstraints b m => MonadNakadiEnv b m | m -> b where
    nakadiAsk :: m (Config' b)
    nakadiReader :: (Config' b -> a) -> m a
```

- Implement `MonadNakadiEnv` for `NakadiT`

- Implement `MonadNakadiEnv` for monad transformers on top of `NakadiT`, in particular `ReaderT` and `ResourceT`. 

- Let the API for the '*R' calls require this type class constraint. For example:

```
eventTypesListR :: MonadNakadiEnv b m => m [EventType]
```

This looks like a rather convenient API. In particular, it does not limit the user to some specific monad stack. Instead, basically any super monad of `b` implementing `MonadNakadiEnv` can be used now.

Why using something like `NakadiT` instead of simply using `ReaderT`?

Because in applications it is common to have a `ReaderT` somewhere in the monad stack. Having two `ReaderT`s in there makes it difficult to use a mtl-style interface like `MonadReader`. Using something distinct like `NakadiT` keeps us totally seperated from `ReaderT`s contained in the application's custom monad stack.

This is what this branch (*parameterize-monad*) is about:

- Generalizing `Config` to `Config b`
- Implementing `MonadSub`, `MonadNakadi` and `MonadNakadiEnv`
- Replacing the `HasNakadiConfig` mechanism with `MonadNakadiEnv`

                     | I propose a (rough sketch for a) language design that I posit while attempting to maintain the most significant opportunities for performance (e.g. monomorphisation) would have superior tradeoffs than Rust in the areas of complexity bloat, design freedom, and benefits versus inflexibility/tsuris of static code analysis. It would have the HLL feel of JavaScript with the LLL control of C++ without all the complexity and unnecessary abstractions (e.g. not the anti-patterns OOP subclassing and not `shared_ptr` as the default over GC).
GC Exclusion Axiom:
Afaics, presuming (enforcement of block scope lifetimes and) all functions input (mutable or immutable because we don’t care in a single-threaded model) borrows—i.e. don’t take lifetime ownership (note callbacks take lifetime ownership)—then GC is not required for provable use-after-free (aka dangling reference/pointer) safety. However, for dynamic data structures that share references (e.g. directed graphs with in-degree > 1), then GC references are much more convenient and performant than the alternative of representing the references with array indices. Note functions that would otherwise take ownership can take ownership of a (GC referenced or unboxed¹) deep copy/clone instead. However where deep cloning would be too costly in terms of performance and memory consumption, shared GC references may be preferred. Where GC is employed we have protection against memory leaks which Rust does not provide, except with an inferior except prompt/deterministic reference counting smart pointer paradigm Rc<T>.
Afaics, there are some marvelous simplifying implications of this axiom: 1. Presuming all functions adhere except where they declare references to be GC, afaics the compiler can _automatically_ implement RAII (in `try-finally` blocks² with an equivalent `finally` [concept for](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-318685944) `Promise` callbacks) for deterministic memory deallocation (and _automatically_ deterministically destruct instances of a type that have a destructor¹ which is [a major feature lacking from GC languages](http://blog.skylight.io/rust-means-never-having-to-close-a-socket/#theownershipsystem) and the `with` of Python being inferior because it is manual and [object isn’t deallocated deterministically](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5071121/raii-in-python-automatic-destruction-when-leaving-a-scope); noting that such types can not used with GC references directly or indirectly as a member of a data structure that is GC referenced). 2. Afaics, the same code will be sound and applicable whether the data structures are implemented by compiler unboxed without GC or boxed with GC. In other words, other than the aforementioned explicit GC references for algorithmic convenience and performance, the programmer never needs to indicate whether the data structures should be boxed or unboxed³. I want to strip away the noise/complexity of `Ref<>`, `Box<>`, etc.. For read-only inputs (i.e. the unannotated default) the programmer need not even think about whether the inputs are cloned-by-value (i.e. primitive type) or passed-by-reference; and cloned-by-value type inputs should never be allowed to be annotated as mutable on the function signature (although they can be mutated inside the function body unless they explicitly annotated read-only and the point being that the programmer never needs to think about whether the type is primitive or not and can see if there is a mutability implication by looking at the function signature). Although I presume an optimizing compiler will always strive for unboxed (because this will be more performant), if we start writing code in say TypeScript we can strive to adhere to this pattern (or have our compiler generate TypeScript) without all the unboxing mess if we so desire. 3. Goodbye to Rust’s lifetime parameters and 3 kinds of pointers noise/tsuris/complexity; and [due to the proposed single-threaded _concurrency_ event model](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-315656536) goodbye also to Rust’s mutability borrowing restrictions/complexity/tsuris. 4. When thinking about interfacing with ASM.js (or Webassembly aka WASM) with minimum (or no) marshaling overhead, then since (which IMO is a [major paradigmatic flaw](http://mrale.ph/blog/2013/03/28/why-asmjs-bothers-me.html#odinmonkey-makes-javascript-fast-with-insane-optimizations)) there is no way yet to have those [interact directly with GC references](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17564972/handwriting-asm-js-how-can-you-track-javascript-objects-in-the-heap) (ostensibly because since there is no static typing then JavaScript thinks these are unbounded polymorphic, i.e. `Any` aka `Object`), we can (until some future where we write our own VM) favor unboxed and [`malloc`ing these via Emscripten](https://kripken.github.io/emscripten-site/docs/porting/connecting_cpp_and_javascript/Interacting-with-code.html#access-memory-from-javascript) (or similar transpilation to ASM.js/WASM of our own C-like language features). ¹ But not cloning resources such as file handles. ² And [Rust’s error handling](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/second-edition/ch09-00-error-handling.html) has no `try` (`panic!` is doesn't `throw` an error up the stack call hierarchy) and instead forces all exceptions to be bubbled up as [`Result`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/second-edition/ch09-02-recoverable-errors-with-result.html) return values which is excessive boilerplate noise/tsuris. ³ Even arrays of data structures that have variable sized members such as `String` can be cleverly implemented (by a library or the compiler) to use indices byte offsets into a second array which contains the variable sized values. This can even work with mutable variable size values, by creating a new value at the end of the second array growing the array as necessary and/or implementing a `malloc` and `free` on the second array, i.e. this second array heap is freed from the parent heap as a monolith. Note if the second array is encapsulated so it can never be referenced directly, then it can be repositioned in virtual address space as needed to minimize virtual address space fragmentation. Monomorphisation could make such libraries more efficient. Note _bounded_ polymorphism never absolutely requires boxing. Unbounded polymorphism would but we are refusing to support `Any`, i.e. all unbounded polymorphism in modules must be bounded when consumed by compiled/linked code. Subsequent discussion in this thread will explain further the rough sketch so that readers can gain clarity. Let’s see what caveats and flaws are revealed via discussion. I look forward to @keean’s feedback and perhaps he will explain to what degree it corresponds to some features of the Ada PL. I do not claim any of these ideas are novel inventions. @keean has alluded to for example cloning as an alternative to lifetimes and/or GC. What I am doing above is making a more holistic presentation of various ideas that have been floating around. Of course [typeclasses or ML functor/modules](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/14#issuecomment-308722477) on top of this for HLL abstractions. If typeclasses, there is [an option to go with implicit function arguments](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/30#issuecomment-302123983) instead of `requires`, which makes it more readily implementable in TypeScript. @shelby [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-315656536): > My expectation is that in Rust the programmer will often need to resort to unsafe code to obtain the necessary freedom. My overriding concern is the K.I.S.S. principle and the amount of the complexity budget consumed for the benefits attained. @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/34#issuecomment-315576966): > …the goals that one justifies employing static typing (“_better structure/abstraction, have more readable/maintainable code, and giving stronger guarantees about safety, lack of bugs, and lack of exploits_”)… > > A valid argument against static typing which I have made on these issues threads, is that no static abstraction can be 100% leak-free. Meaning that eventually we always end up having to violate the invariants of the abstraction, or moreover that it becomes very convoluted to maintain type safety and have complete degrees-of-freedom of expression. So then static typing becomes a negative factor for productivity instead of a positive one. This is why selecting which abstractions to enforce with a compiler is an engineering design challenge (arguably even perhaps an art) of matching to use cases. @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-313808940): > …there is diminishing return from static checking complexity because we can not statically check every clever algorithm and design paradigm that programmers will come up with. I think he had mentioned fighting with type systems. > > I am interested to explore static typing that does not frustrate programmers. > … > Disagree that Rust’s balance of flexibility and tsuris is ideally suited to most apps. @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-313713206): > Additionally it’s the noise of extreme static checking such as the lifetime parameters (in addition to generic parameters and normal kinds of static types) on every function in Rust… GC is so much more elegant. I understand certain real-time use cases will not tolerate GC pauses (although we did also discuss V8’s incremental mark-and-sweep upthread) and more optimized by zero overhead abstractions (e.g. no runtime overhead for deciding which to deallocate) @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-313578132): > Perhaps we will eventually think of some low-complexity abstraction that gives us non-marshaled integration for tree data structures between HLL and LLL, and perhaps we can even prove borrowing and lifetimes statically. But I suspect we can not without heading towards the complexity of C++ and Rust. @keean [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-312874353): > I would not write a web service in 'C' or even 'Rust' ever, this is really ideal ground for a garbage collected language. I would use Node (TypeScript), Django(Python) or 'Go'. @keean [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-312443168): > My view is there needs to be a high-level-language and a low-level-language that share enough memory-layout and data-structure that data can easily be passed backward and forward. @shelby3 wrote: > I am wanting to move away from such clusterfucks of never ending aggregation of complexity. > I am not going to try to argue that Rust has no use cases. > > But I want to create a mainstream programming language used by millions of programmers. > > Do you want to compete with Rust? @keean [replied](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-312446734): > @shelby3 wrote: >> Once we start heading for Rust’s three different kinds of pointers, then I will think we have failed to make a clean high-level language for the masses. > > Here we agree."},"comment":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript/issues/comments/354648164","html_url":"https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/35#issuecomment-354648164","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript/issues/35","id":354648164,"user":{"login":"keean","id":508384,"avatar_url":"https://avatars2.githubusercontent.com/u/508384?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean","html_url":"https://github.com/keean","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/keean/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2018-01-01T11:15:34Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:15:34Z","author_association":"OWNER","body":"> "}}

is a  OpenHAB 2 port of the existing 1.x Denon binding (created by @idserda). As the binding supports both Denon and Marantz receivers decided to change the name to  'denonmarantz'.

Improvements:
- support for Discovery (MDNS)
- defined channels (including an 'advanced' Channel to send any custom command)
- improved Telnet stability (although that has been addressed in the old binding)

Note that this binding is still work in progress. Need others to test this binding as I only own one Marantz receiver (SR5008) myself. That is the main reason for this PR, as I know some cleanup, fixing and documentation is required.

This is my first binding, and it took more time and effort than I'd hoped for.. ;)
Happy to learn how to further improve.

Description

Allows fallback videos to be used for download, when the main video URL is not downloadable (e.g., HLS .m3u8).

**JIRA**

[OSPR-2019](https://openedx.atlassian.net/browse/OSPR-2019)

Allows the streaming video URL to differ from the download URL.  Iterates through the `all_sources` HTML5 video URLs to locate a downloadable video URL, if the streaming video URL is not downloadable.

### Notes

Functionality depends on API changes in https://github.com/edx/edx-platform/pull/16590, but the app continues to work even if this change is not deployed yet.

Builds on https://github.com/edx/edx-app-ios/pull/1014, which differentiates between streamable and downloadable video URLs.

We'd like to get this merged before the next edx-app-ios release.

### How to test this PR

Ensure that the changes from https://github.com/edx/edx-platform/pull/16590 are running in your LMS, and import this [video_test_course.tar.gz](https://github.com/edx/edx-app-ios/files/1493756/video_test_course.Dl2Kjh.tar.gz), which contains permutations of all the various video streaming/download scenarios.

Alternately, run against this sandbox server, using:
```yaml
API_HOST_URL: 'https://pr16590.sandbox.opencraft.hosting'
OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: '14cdc120d61349b7eeba'
```

1. Run the iOS app.
1. Login as a student to the test course.
1. Visit each of the course subsections in turn, noting the expected Streaming and Download behaviours for each unit below.
    *note* Once you've downloaded a video, that video will be used in the player, regardless of what the original streaming video URL is.  So to test the permutations below, try streaming first, then download.

* YouTube:
    * Standard: YouTube 
        * Streaming: YouTube only; will not play on iOS app, but will play in browser.
        * Download: none
    * Standard w Fallback:  
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 (same as MP4 - 1), different from YouTube video
        * Download: yes, same as stream
    * HLS live stream:
        * Streaming: YouTube only; will not play on iOS app, but will play in browser.
        * Download: none
    * HLS w fallback:
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 (same as MP4 - 1)
            *Note* The main video is configured to use the same YouTube HLS used in the previous unit, but `USING_VIDEO_PIPELINE: false` causes the fallback URL to be streamed instead.
        * Download: Same as stream.
* MP4 
    * MP4 - 1
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
    * MP4 - 1 w fallback
        * Streaming: 0.05 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
            *Note* Fallback video is configured to be the 0:27 mp4 used by MP4 - 2, but because the main video 
            can be downloaded, the fallback video is ignored.
    * MP4 - 2
        * Streaming: 0:27 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
    * MP4 - 2 w fallback
        * Streaming: 0:27 mp4 
        * Download: yes, same as stream
            *note* Fallback video is configured to be the 0:05 mp4 used by MP4 - 1, but because the main video 
            can be downloaded, the fallback video is ignored.
* HLS .m3u8
    * HLS (10 min):
        * Streaming: 10:35 video
        * Download: none
    * HLS (10 min) w fallback:
        * Streaming: 10:35 video
        * Download: 0:27 mp4, same as MP4 - 2
    * Vimeo
        * Streaming: 8:22 Cloudera m3mu
        * Download: none
    * Vimeo w fallback
        * Streaming: 8:22 Cloudera m3mu
        * Download: 8:22 Cloudera mp4

{"action":"reopened","issue":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript/issues/35","repository_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript","labels_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript/issues/35/labels{/name}","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript/issues/35/comments","events_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/keean/zenscript/issues/35/events","html_url":"https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/35","id":243345358,"number":35,"title":"WD-40 (for reducing Rust with the next mainstream language)","user":{"login":"shelby3","id":247731,"avatar_url":"https://avatars3.githubusercontent.com/u/247731?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3","html_url":"https://github.com/shelby3","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/shelby3/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"labels":[],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignee":null,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":100,"created_at":"2017-07-17T09:55:13Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:15:51Z","closed_at":null,"author_association":"NONE","body":"⁣ | ⁣ ----- | ----- ![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/WD-40_Smart_Straw.JPG/103px-WD-40_Smart_Straw.JPG)
                     | I propose a (rough sketch for a) language design that I posit while attempting to maintain the most significant opportunities for performance (e.g. monomorphisation) would have superior tradeoffs than Rust in the areas of complexity bloat, design freedom, and benefits versus inflexibility/tsuris of static code analysis. It would have the HLL feel of JavaScript with the LLL control of C++ without all the complexity and unnecessary abstractions (e.g. not the anti-patterns OOP subclassing and not `shared_ptr` as the default over GC).
GC Exclusion Axiom:
Afaics, presuming (enforcement of block scope lifetimes and) all functions input (mutable or immutable because we don’t care in a single-threaded model) borrows—i.e. don’t take lifetime ownership (note callbacks take lifetime ownership)—then GC is not required for provable use-after-free (aka dangling reference/pointer) safety. However, for dynamic data structures that share references (e.g. directed graphs with in-degree > 1), then GC references are much more convenient and performant than the alternative of representing the references with array indices. Note functions that would otherwise take ownership can take ownership of a (GC referenced or unboxed¹) deep copy/clone instead. However where deep cloning would be too costly in terms of performance and memory consumption, shared GC references may be preferred. Where GC is employed we have protection against memory leaks which Rust does not provide, except with an inferior except prompt/deterministic reference counting smart pointer paradigm Rc<T>.
Afaics, there are some marvelous simplifying implications of this axiom: 1. Presuming all functions adhere except where they declare references to be GC, afaics the compiler can _automatically_ implement RAII (in `try-finally` blocks² with an equivalent `finally` [concept for](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-318685944) `Promise` callbacks) for deterministic memory deallocation (and _automatically_ deterministically destruct instances of a type that have a destructor¹ which is [a major feature lacking from GC languages](http://blog.skylight.io/rust-means-never-having-to-close-a-socket/#theownershipsystem) and the `with` of Python being inferior because it is manual and [object isn’t deallocated deterministically](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5071121/raii-in-python-automatic-destruction-when-leaving-a-scope); noting that such types can not used with GC references directly or indirectly as a member of a data structure that is GC referenced). 2. Afaics, the same code will be sound and applicable whether the data structures are implemented by compiler unboxed without GC or boxed with GC. In other words, other than the aforementioned explicit GC references for algorithmic convenience and performance, the programmer never needs to indicate whether the data structures should be boxed or unboxed³. I want to strip away the noise/complexity of `Ref<>`, `Box<>`, etc.. For read-only inputs (i.e. the unannotated default) the programmer need not even think about whether the inputs are cloned-by-value (i.e. primitive type) or passed-by-reference; and cloned-by-value type inputs should never be allowed to be annotated as mutable on the function signature (although they can be mutated inside the function body unless they explicitly annotated read-only and the point being that the programmer never needs to think about whether the type is primitive or not and can see if there is a mutability implication by looking at the function signature). Although I presume an optimizing compiler will always strive for unboxed (because this will be more performant), if we start writing code in say TypeScript we can strive to adhere to this pattern (or have our compiler generate TypeScript) without all the unboxing mess if we so desire. 3. Goodbye to Rust’s lifetime parameters and 3 kinds of pointers noise/tsuris/complexity; and [due to the proposed single-threaded _concurrency_ event model](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-315656536) goodbye also to Rust’s mutability borrowing restrictions/complexity/tsuris. 4. When thinking about interfacing with ASM.js (or Webassembly aka WASM) with minimum (or no) marshaling overhead, then since (which IMO is a [major paradigmatic flaw](http://mrale.ph/blog/2013/03/28/why-asmjs-bothers-me.html#odinmonkey-makes-javascript-fast-with-insane-optimizations)) there is no way yet to have those [interact directly with GC references](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17564972/handwriting-asm-js-how-can-you-track-javascript-objects-in-the-heap) (ostensibly because since there is no static typing then JavaScript thinks these are unbounded polymorphic, i.e. `Any` aka `Object`), we can (until some future where we write our own VM) favor unboxed and [`malloc`ing these via Emscripten](https://kripken.github.io/emscripten-site/docs/porting/connecting_cpp_and_javascript/Interacting-with-code.html#access-memory-from-javascript) (or similar transpilation to ASM.js/WASM of our own C-like language features). ¹ But not cloning resources such as file handles. ² And [Rust’s error handling](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/second-edition/ch09-00-error-handling.html) has no `try` (`panic!` is doesn't `throw` an error up the stack call hierarchy) and instead forces all exceptions to be bubbled up as [`Result`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/second-edition/ch09-02-recoverable-errors-with-result.html) return values which is excessive boilerplate noise/tsuris. ³ Even arrays of data structures that have variable sized members such as `String` can be cleverly implemented (by a library or the compiler) to use indices byte offsets into a second array which contains the variable sized values. This can even work with mutable variable size values, by creating a new value at the end of the second array growing the array as necessary and/or implementing a `malloc` and `free` on the second array, i.e. this second array heap is freed from the parent heap as a monolith. Note if the second array is encapsulated so it can never be referenced directly, then it can be repositioned in virtual address space as needed to minimize virtual address space fragmentation. Monomorphisation could make such libraries more efficient. Note _bounded_ polymorphism never absolutely requires boxing. Unbounded polymorphism would but we are refusing to support `Any`, i.e. all unbounded polymorphism in modules must be bounded when consumed by compiled/linked code. Subsequent discussion in this thread will explain further the rough sketch so that readers can gain clarity. Let’s see what caveats and flaws are revealed via discussion. I look forward to @keean’s feedback and perhaps he will explain to what degree it corresponds to some features of the Ada PL. I do not claim any of these ideas are novel inventions. @keean has alluded to for example cloning as an alternative to lifetimes and/or GC. What I am doing above is making a more holistic presentation of various ideas that have been floating around. Of course [typeclasses or ML functor/modules](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/14#issuecomment-308722477) on top of this for HLL abstractions. If typeclasses, there is [an option to go with implicit function arguments](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/30#issuecomment-302123983) instead of `requires`, which makes it more readily implementable in TypeScript. @shelby [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-315656536): > My expectation is that in Rust the programmer will often need to resort to unsafe code to obtain the necessary freedom. My overriding concern is the K.I.S.S. principle and the amount of the complexity budget consumed for the benefits attained. @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/34#issuecomment-315576966): > …the goals that one justifies employing static typing (“_better structure/abstraction, have more readable/maintainable code, and giving stronger guarantees about safety, lack of bugs, and lack of exploits_”)… > > A valid argument against static typing which I have made on these issues threads, is that no static abstraction can be 100% leak-free. Meaning that eventually we always end up having to violate the invariants of the abstraction, or moreover that it becomes very convoluted to maintain type safety and have complete degrees-of-freedom of expression. So then static typing becomes a negative factor for productivity instead of a positive one. This is why selecting which abstractions to enforce with a compiler is an engineering design challenge (arguably even perhaps an art) of matching to use cases. @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-313808940): > …there is diminishing return from static checking complexity because we can not statically check every clever algorithm and design paradigm that programmers will come up with. I think he had mentioned fighting with type systems. > > I am interested to explore static typing that does not frustrate programmers. > … > Disagree that Rust’s balance of flexibility and tsuris is ideally suited to most apps. @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-313713206): > Additionally it’s the noise of extreme static checking such as the lifetime parameters (in addition to generic parameters and normal kinds of static types) on every function in Rust… GC is so much more elegant. I understand certain real-time use cases will not tolerate GC pauses (although we did also discuss V8’s incremental mark-and-sweep upthread) and more optimized by zero overhead abstractions (e.g. no runtime overhead for deciding which to deallocate) @shelby3 [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-313578132): > Perhaps we will eventually think of some low-complexity abstraction that gives us non-marshaled integration for tree data structures between HLL and LLL, and perhaps we can even prove borrowing and lifetimes statically. But I suspect we can not without heading towards the complexity of C++ and Rust. @keean [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-312874353): > I would not write a web service in 'C' or even 'Rust' ever, this is really ideal ground for a garbage collected language. I would use Node (TypeScript), Django(Python) or 'Go'. @keean [wrote](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-312443168): > My view is there needs to be a high-level-language and a low-level-language that share enough memory-layout and data-structure that data can easily be passed backward and forward. @shelby3 wrote: > I am wanting to move away from such clusterfucks of never ending aggregation of complexity. > I am not going to try to argue that Rust has no use cases. > > But I want to create a mainstream programming language used by millions of programmers. > > Do you want to compete with Rust? @keean [replied](https://github.com/keean/zenscript/issues/17#issuecomment-312446734): > @shelby3 wrote: >> Once we start heading for Rust’s three different kinds of pointers, then I will think we have failed to make a clean high-level language for the masses. > > Here we agree."}}

    _.round(89.6849593495935, 2) === 89.69

but actually

    _.round(89.6849593495935, 2) === 89.68

This is not a contrived issue, the problem arose while calculating taxes with Lodash and feeding the results to government forms that reported errors in calculations.

made some minor changes:

- No longer catches all exceptions, but gives them to NLog (NLog uses the exception to notify wrappers about failures)
- Added more logging about failures, so they can be monitored in NLog-InternalLogger.
- Fixed the nuget-package so it correctly uses MsgPack.Cli ver. 0.8.0 (Instead of ver. 0.4.1)
- Removed allocation of SerializationContext for every message property

I'm trying to test a class that can be optionally initialized with environment variables.  The code functions as expected when passing env vars from the command line or if set during an interactive session, but fails under pytest.  I'm using monkeypatch to set the `host` and `port` values during tests.

Strangely, if I set the values during instance initialization from within the `__init__` method (as opposed to via args) the tests pass.

I'm not sure if this is a bug or if I'm making some mistake in how the tests are written.

I included two examples below to illustrate the passing and failing cases.  The `class_init_env_1.py` code and associated test set the environment variables in method arguments, and this test fails (see output below).

The `class_init_env_2.py` code and associated test set the environment variables within the `__init__` method, and this test passes (see output below).

If I run either via the commands below, the output is identical and functions as expected:
```SERVICE_HOST=server2 SERVICE_PORT=12345 python class_init_env_1.py```
```SERVICE_HOST=server2 SERVICE_PORT=12345 python class_init_env_2.py```

# class_init_env_1.py

import os


class Example:
    def __init__(self,
                 host=os.environ.get('SERVICE_HOST', 'localhost'),
                 port=os.environ.get('SERVICE_PORT', 30650)):

        self.host = host
        self.port = port

    example = Example()
    print(example.host)
    print(example.port)

main()

```python
# test_class_init_env_1.py

import os
from class_init_env_1 import Example
import pytest


def test_class_init_with_env_vars(monkeypatch):
    # GIVEN environment variables are set for host and port
    monkeypatch.setenv('SERVICE_HOST', 'server.example.com')
    monkeypatch.setenv('SERVICE_PORT', '12345')
    #   AND a class instance is initialized without specifying a host or port
    example = Example()
    # THEN the instance should reflect the host and port specified in the environment variables
    assert example.host == 'server.example.com'
    assert example.port == '12345'
```

Various instances of duplication. See current `dupreport`:

https://gist.github.com/naiveaiguy/1eb8a12f2aa75876a1729d6f0bff1c10

Extracts methods that abstract out the functionality of these duplicates. I've tried as much as possible to keep each commit sensible and working, so any of these can be reverted individually relatively cleanly if the need arises.

* package.json - `dupreport` script

-Volume steps changes are instant, no need to reboot!

LiveVolumeSteps: transitioned volume steps volume normalization.

-This calculates an equivalent volume ratio for the new
volume steps.
-example: Volume steps are set at 60. Volume is set at 5. That is
very low volume. Then volume steps are switched to 5. Now you
are instantly in a state were your volume steps are 5 and your
volume is 5. That's full volume! This fixes that issue.
-So it basically keeps the volume from jumping around while your
changing volume steps. It may be a little lower but should be
very close.

while-let-chains","user":{"login":"Centril","id":855702,"avatar_url":"https://avatars2.githubusercontent.com/u/855702?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril","html_url":"https://github.com/Centril","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Centril/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"labels":[{"id":211667886,"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/rust-lang/rfcs/labels/T-lang","name":"T-lang","color":"bfd4f2","default":false}],"state":"open","locked":false,"assignee":null,"assignees":[],"milestone":null,"comments":137,"created_at":"2017-12-24T02:28:28Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:17:31Z","closed_at":null,"author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","pull_request":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/rust-lang/rfcs/pulls/2260","html_url":"https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260","diff_url":"https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260.diff","patch_url":"https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260.patch"},"body":"[Rendered](https://github.com/Centril/rfcs/blob/rfc/let-chains/text/0000-let-chains.md)

This RFC was co-authored with @scottmcm ;)

----------------

Here's a survey on some choices of syntax.
Please answer it if you have the time.
And please don't spread the survey around.

https://goo.gl/forms/Wx61sx9s03N5SGA52

-----------------

Before considering this RFC, please remember what is most important: reducing rightward drift and improving ergonomics in control flow. The exact syntax can always be changed into a direction you prefer. If you don't like the syntax, please write a comment about that below or agree with someone who has put forth your view. Thank you :)

**EDIT: The exact syntax regarding `&&` or `,` or chaining `if` is very much in flux right now.**

-----------------

This RFC extends `if let`- and `while let`-expressions with chaining, allowing
you to combining multiple `let`s and conditions together naturally. With this
RFC implemented, you will, among other things, now be able to write:

```rust
/// Returns the slice of format string parts in an `Arguments::new_v1` call.
fn get_argument_fmtstr_parts(expr: &Expr) -> Option<(InternedString, usize)> {
    if let ExprAddrOf(_, ref expr) = expr.node // &["…", "…", …]
     , let ExprArray(ref exprs) = expr.node
     , let Some(expr) = exprs.last()
     , let ExprLit(ref lit) = expr.node
     , let LitKind::Str(ref lit, _) = lit.node {
        Some((lit.as_str(), exprs.len()))
    } else {
        None
    }
}
```"},"comment":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/rust-lang/rfcs/issues/comments/354648225","html_url":"https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260#issuecomment-354648225","issue_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/rust-lang/rfcs/issues/2260","id":354648225,"user":{"login":"petrochenkov","id":5751617,"avatar_url":"https://avatars2.githubusercontent.com/u/5751617?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov","html_url":"https://github.com/petrochenkov","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/petrochenkov/received_events","type":"User","site_admin":false},"created_at":"2018-01-01T11:17:31Z","updated_at":"2018-01-01T11:17:31Z","author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","body":"Some larger picture of syntactic ambiguities:
1. Syntax "guarded from both sides". `prefix EXPR op PAT suffix` / `prefix PAT op EXPT suffix` won't hit any ambiguities, but it's basically equivalent to "always use parentheses" - `(EXPR op PAT)` / `(prefix PAT op EXPT)`.
2. Syntax "guarded from the start". `prefix EXPR op PAT` has unnecessary `prefix` and hits "no struct literal restriction" in some contexts. `prefix PAT op EXPR` hits ambiguities like `let x = y && z` (https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260#issuecomment-354580296).
3. Syntax "guarded from the end". `EXPR op PAT suffix` won't hit any ambiguities (I'm not sure what specific `suffix` would be appropriate here though). `PAT op EXPR suffix` has ambiguity expr vs pattern at the start (https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260#issuecomment-354104547).
4. Syntax "not guarded". `EXPR op PAT` hits "no struct literal restriction" in some contexts. `PAT op EXPR` has ambiguity expr vs pattern at the start (https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2260#issuecomment-354104547).

Looks like "no struct literal restriction" is the least evil here, unless we come up with some `EXPR op PAT suffix` syntax looking more reasonable than parens `(EXPR op PAT)`."}}

## Tietosisältö ja -kanta
Tietosisältö täyttää vaatimukset: monesta-moneen suhde, kaksi CRUD-nelikkoa, kolme tietokohdetta löytyvät.

[Taulujen luontikyselyissä](https://github.com/vvenla/Tsoha-Bootstrap/blob/master/sql/create_tables.sql#L7-L18) `Tehtava`-luokka pitäisi varmaan luoda `Luokka`-luokan jälkeen, sillä `Tehtava`:n `luokkaId` viittaa `Luokka`:n `id`-kenttään.

Lisäksi testidataa voisi hieman laajentaa lisäämällä esimerkiksi toisen käyttäjän ja jaettuja tehtäviä.

## HTML ja ulkoasu
Ulkoasu on selkeä ja HTML-tiedostot vaikuttavat pääosin hyviltä.

[paanakyma.html](https://github.com/vvenla/Tsoha-Bootstrap/blob/master/app/views/suunnitelmat/paanakyma.html#L20-L21):ssä rivien 20 ja 21 välistä taitaa puuttua sulkeva `td`-tagi.

Luettavuuden kannalta olisi hyvä laittaa avaava ja sulkeva tagi joko molemmat samalle riville tai molemmat omille riveilleen. [tehtavanLisays.html](https://github.com/vvenla/Tsoha-Bootstrap/blob/master/app/views/suunnitelmat/tehtavanLisays.html#L20-L21):n riveillä 20-21 oleva nappi on hieman hankala lukea."}}

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug


**What happened**:
--cloud-provider=aws in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml makes it fail to start with CrashLoopBackOff.

### kube-controller-manager.yaml 

    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: kube-controller-manager
      namespace: kube-system
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - kube-controller-manager
        - --leader-elect=true
        - --use-service-account-credentials=true
        - --controllers=*,bootstrapsigner,tokencleaner
        - --root-ca-file=/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt
        - --cluster-signing-cert-file=/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt
        - --cluster-signing-key-file=/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key
        - --address=127.0.0.1
        - --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/controller-manager.conf
        - --service-account-private-key-file=/etc/kubernetes/pki/sa.key
        - --allocate-node-cidrs=true
        - --cluster-cidr=10.244.0.0/16
        - --node-cidr-mask-size=24
        - --cloud-provider=aws     <----- (without this line, no issue)

### Pod state

    kube-system   kube-controller-manager-ip-172-31-4-117.us-west-1.compute.internal   0/1       CrashLoopBackOff   2          34s
